evidence_policy.byte_proof: chat-a-grndat-byte-audit.json checks the entire 600-instruction GRNDAT case and 118 direct branches against PE bytes, plus focused helper disassemblies and format strings. It includes shared material-selection prefix and return epilogue. This establishes static control flow, not successful runtime execution.
evidence_policy.offsets: All material offsets are bytes from the selected native material base M. Record/table/list offsets are relative to explicitly named bases. Integer fields are int32, pointers are 64-bit, doubles are binary64. Unwritten padding is not zero-filled by assumption.

entry_and_status.material_selection: Before the GRNDAT case, fscanf("%i") selects the material ID. EOF returns2. A missing material is constructed and linked, its ID and root material count are stored, and 0x1401d0fc0(root,1) runs before the outer GRNDAT header. Thus a later early return can still follow a creation refresh. A matching failure (conversion count0) leaves an uninitialized selector local; that unsupported domain must not be assigned deterministic material selection.

outer_header.grammar: One fgets(buffer,1024) line; replace commas with spaces; sscanf("%i %i") into two locals zeroed by the helper.
outer_header.failure: fgets EOF or sscanf -1 returns helper1, dispatcher2, before storing M+0x17e8. Existing material GRNDAT fields remain unchanged. Creation effects above survive.
outer_header.partial: sscanf0 or1 is success: missing values remain0. Successful outer header stores its first int at M+0x17e8 before any branch payload.
outer_header.secondary: Second int is stored only for selector2 at M+0x14d0. It is not the negative-selector field M+0x17ec.

entry_and_status.return_mapping: Dispatcher returns0 if retained local helper status is0, otherwise2. Record/table/line helpers here return0/1. No transactional rollback.

refresh.preserves_status: Caller retains helper status in [rsp+0x100] across refresh; common epilogue maps it to0/2.
reached: Selector1 after all nine payloads succeeded: refresh even if its final pair reader fails
Selector2 after the initial record and every actually appended record succeed; ignored list-count failures do not prevent refresh
Selector4 after table reader success or failure
Selector5 after coefficient reader success or failure
Zero, 3, unknown positive, and negative selectors after successful outer header
skipped: Selector1 failure at any of nine headers or nine payloads
Selector2 failure while reading any appended record
refresh.qualification: This describes the postbranch refresh. New-material creation can already have run option1. A helper fault, allocation failure or nontermination is not a normal returned status.

selector1.order: Read/reset all nine table headers first, then read all nine payloads in the same order, then the final pair.
header_effects: 0x140413ee0 reads subselector and count into zeroed locals. Failure returns2 before resetting that table; earlier table resets and flag changes survive, while this and later tables retain old state.

On success 0x14012fc70(table,type) resets common typed metadata and owned arrays while retaining table+0x54 and table+0x60. It does not reset table+0x68. Then subselector1 sets axis selector0=3; subselector2 sets it8; supported subselector3 sets it33. Unsupported values retain the reset default3.

For flagged tables, subselector0 writes flag0; subselector1/2 writes flag1; table+0x1448 also writes flag1 for3. Other subselectors retain the previous flag. A disabled flag does not skip payload reading.

Store raw parsed count at table+0x1c after reset. Negative count is retained until payload allocation clamps it0. The constructor/reset type profiles have rank1 and the per-table width above; their zero counts produce null axes/dependent buffers.
selector1.payload: Each 0x14041a800(FILE*,table,0) replaces/zeroes the table's storage then reads rank1 rows: axis0 followed by width dependent values per point. EOF returns1, translated immediately to2 with no postbranch refresh. Conversion0 leaves the zeroed destination unchanged and continues. All nine headers have already reset all nine tables when the first payload begins. After a completed payload, a positive total triggers one ignored-result fgets1024 to discard the current line remainder.
selector1.partial_mutation: Header failure preserves failed/later tables; payload failure leaves all nine reset, earlier tables filled, current prefix filled, and later tables reset but unfilled. Prefix mutations are not undone.

final_pair.behavior: Both live doubles are zeroed before one comma-normalized line scan. Assigned prefix survives; EOF/scan-1 leaves zero/partial values and returns1. Postbranch refresh always follows this call; dispatcher returns0/2 from its status.

selector2.initial: Store outer secondary at M+0x14d0, then call 0x14041bed0(FILE*,M+0x14d8) at0x140387574. Any failure returns2 before any list is cleared; secondary and partial initial-record changes survive. Its flag+0x1e0 remains1 from construction, so it reads only its third table.
per_list: Clear that list through0x14028b240 before reading its replacement count.

Read count with0x140413de0(FILE*,&local_count,1); helper zeroes count and reads one line, skipping at most one exact single-LF line, then comma-normalized sscanf%i. Its returned status is ignored; EOF/blank/matching failure ordinarily leaves count0. Negative count produces zero loop iterations.
For i=0 while i<count: append a constructed0x1f0 record through0x14028b050 before calling0x14041bed0 on it. Constructor flag+0x1e0=0, so it reads all three nested tables.

Any record failure returns2 immediately: failed node remains linked and counted with its partial fields. Earlier replacement lists remain; later untouched lists retain old contents. Successful record reads reset retained local status0.
selector2.completion: If no record fails, all five lists are visited and postbranch refresh runs with status0, even if one or all count readers failed. EOF immediately after a successful initial record can therefore clear all five lists and return0.

record_reader.ABI: RCX=FILE*, RDX=record. Extra pseudocode parameters are not a recovered input contract.

layout.0x08..0x60: fixed inline array of twelve doubles; fresh+0
layout.0x1e0: byte skip-first-two-tables; fresh node0, embedded initial record1

steps: Set local count0, then direct stream fscanf%i. Only result-1 returns1 before changing the record. Matching failure0 proceeds with count0.

0x14029ccd0 clamps only counts>12 to12, mutates the local count as well as record+0, and emits the diagnostic 'Error - SubbdryVarSize is incorrect.\n'. It does not clamp negative values or set failure status. There is no variable-array allocation.

Read exactly the clamped positive count stream doubles directly to record+8+8*i. Only-1 aborts1. Values beyond the selected prefix retain old contents; matching failure leaves each destination unchanged. Excess input beyond a declared>12 count is not discarded and can become subsequent fields.

Direct stream fscanf("%i %Flf") writes record+0x70 first, then+0x68. It does not zero those live fields. Only aggregate-1 returns1; a partial or zero conversion is success and retains unassigned fields.
If record byte+0x1e0==0, call0x14041c070 on table+0x78 then+0xf0, aborting1 after each nonzero result. If byte is nonzero, skip both without mutation or input consumption.
Always call0x14041c070 on+0x168 last. Map its zero/nonzero result to0/1.
record_reader.input_domain: The count and inline-double/scalar-pair scans are direct fscanf calls: they cross whitespace/newlines and do not perform the line helper's comma normalization. Preserve the retained legacy scanner contract, not the host's unrestricted numeric parser.
record_reader.failure_effects: The embedded record is updated in place without reset; a fresh appended record starts initialized. Neither reader failures nor selector changes destroy already imported subrecords.

nested_record_table_reader.different_from: This is not0x14041b270. It performs no typed reset and never uses sscanf's conversion count to reject a line.
nested_record_table_reader.header: Initialize local selector=-1 and three doubles=+0; fgets1024; on exactly one LF-only line, read once more. EOF at either read returns1 without table mutation. Replace commas by spaces and scan%i %Flf %Flf %Flf. The fourth numeric item is read into a local but unused.

selector_effects.writes: No header field writes; existing shape is reused

nested_record_table_reader.payload: For any parsed selector>0 call0x14041a800(FILE*,table,0) and return its result. Otherwise return0. Blank second lines, whitespace-only lines and matching failures leave selector-1 and therefore can return0 while retaining the table.
nested_record_table_reader.retention: Type, width, flags, other selectors/counts, cache and padding remain unless the payload allocator changes its own fields. Selector0 changes rank/constant without freeing old arrays or clearing old counts. Later positive imports can therefore encounter retained shape/ownership metadata.
nested_record_table_reader.conversion: Assembly uses CVTTSD2SI to int32 for count fields. For bounded finite in-range values, this is truncation toward zero. Nonfinite/out-of-range conversions and FP exception controls remain outside the proposed compatibility profile.
nested_record_table_reader.payload_rank1: Direct prefix mutation of zeroed allocated axes/dependent values; conversion0 does not abort; EOF1 retains prefix.
nested_record_table_reader.payload_rank2: Read axis0 then axis1 directly. Read dependent values into uninitialized temporary scratch; copy the whole scratch only after every scan avoids EOF, then free it. Scratch EOF leaves dependent zeros and leaks native scratch. Matching failures can later copy unwritten scratch bytes, so require explicit unknown-byte handling or exclude that domain.
nested_record_table_reader.line_consumption: The payload consumes a final fgets1024 only when its computed dependent count>0; ignored EOF there preserves success. Zero-sized tables consume no final discard.

0x14028b640 at M+0x14d0 constructs record+8, then five lists at relative0x1f8/0x210/0x228/0x240/0x258. It zeroes its leading int and explicitly sets embedded-record byte+0x1e0=1.

0x14028a4c0 constructs record tables+0x78/+0xf0/+0x168, sets next+0x1e8=null, then0x14028a580 resets tables to94/95/96, writes count12, zeros twelve inline doubles and scalar+0x68/int+0x70, and sets byte+0x1e0=0. These table types start rank0, width1, constant+0, counts/selectors0, arrays/cache null.

0x14028af00 zeros list head+0, tail+8 and int32 count+0x10. The0x18-byte list stride includes unproved padding+0x14..0x17. Ghidra's COleControlSiteOrWnd library match is not used as semantic identity.
ownership_and_initialization.append: 0x14028b050 allocates0x1f0 bytes, runs0x14028a4c0, links at tail via old_tail+0x1e8 (or sets both head/tail for count0), increments list+0x10, returns node. It does not wait for parsing to succeed. Allocation failure is not converted into a clean importer error and is outside the bounded contract.
ownership_and_initialization.clear: 0x14028b240 follows head untilnull, saves next+0x1e8 before destroying node through0x14029cd60(node,1), then zeros head/tail/count.0x14029cd60 calls record destructor0x14028a530 thenfree when flagbit0 is set.
ownership_and_initialization.record_destroy: 0x14028a530 destroys nested tables in reverse order+0x168,+0xf0,+0x78 through0x14012f410. Inline array/scalars have no separate allocation; nodefree occurs only in deleting wrapper.
ownership_and_initialization.group_destroy: 0x14028b8e0: no-op coefficient destructor0x14028a4b0(group+0x740), selector4 table destructor0x14028a420(group+0x6c8), selector2 group destructor0x14028b6f0(group+0x458), nine-table destructor0x14028a320(group). Selector2 group clears lists in reverse layout order M+0x1728,0x1710,0x16f8,0x16e0,0x16c8, then destroys embedded record without freeing it separately. Nine tables are destroyed from M+0x1448 down to0x1088.
ownership_and_initialization.table_ownership: 0x14012f410 calls0x14012f480 for axes/dependent allocations and deletes nonnull cache+0x68 through0x14013c170(pointer,1). This pass uses the owned, null-cache constructor/import profile. Generic clear suppresses all frees if any axis has count0 but a nonnull pointer, then nulls pointers; negative-count axis frees are also suppressed. Do not silently claim ordinary vector cleanup reproduces every native resource lifetime.
ownership_and_initialization.lifecycle_scope: Ordinary material-default routine0x14028cdc0 does not reconstruct this nested group; unrelated edits/selector switches retain it. Whole material destruction and dimension-reset destruction release it. Fresh material construction reinstates the defaults. Copy/shared alias paths and nonnull-cache producers are not recovered here.

selector4_preserved.contract: Preserve the existing selector4 implementation/contract: zeroed local header fields, comma-normalized line, failed header preserves old table; successful header applies generic type0 reset while preserving54/60, selector profile and shared payload reader. Always execute postbranch refresh even if table helper returns1; dispatcher then returns2.
selector4_preserved.runtime_limit: Only prior bounded selector4 cohorts provide runtime corroboration here; they ran with root+0x864=0. This static pass neither broadens nor replaces that claim.

selector5.ABI: FILE in RCX; first three double* in RDX/R8/R9; remaining three at caller stack+0x20/+0x28/+0x30. The helper supplies all six pointers to sscanf through registers and stack.
selector5.behavior: Zero all six live outputs before fgets1024. No blank-line skip. Replace commas with spaces; scan six%Flf fields. EOF or scan-1 returns1; any nonnegative conversion count returns0. Partial assignments survive with zero remainder. Negative zero is preserved if assigned.
selector5.refresh: Status store at0x14038799c precedes unconditional postbranch refresh; return is0 or2. Other GRNDAT branches/tables remain retained.

other_selectors.zero_three_unknown_positive: After successful outer header store raw selector at M+0x17e8, consume no branch payload, leave other fields unchanged, refresh(root,0), return0.
other_selectors.negative: At0x1403879b6 bytesf7d9 execute NEG ECX. Store the modulo2^32 negated bit pattern at M+0x17ec and store-1 at M+0x17e8; no payload, refresh, return0. INT_MIN remains0x80000000 in17ec; overflow flag is not branched on. Portable code must use explicit 32-bit bit arithmetic instead of signed-C++ negation overflow.
other_selectors.retained_negative_field: A subsequent nonnegative selector does not clear17ec.
